description: Numeric literals are typed from their text: a fractional literal is decimal, an exponent literal is float64, and a small plain integer literal is int32, matching PostgreSQL's own literal typing

columns.name: whole
columns.note: a small integer literal is int32 in PostgreSQL (pg_typeof(1) is integer, not bigint)

columns.name: half
columns.note: a fractional literal is decimal in PostgreSQL, not int32/int64

columns.name: huge
columns.note: exponent notation is double precision in PostgreSQL

name: fractional_and_exponent_literals
query_sql:
-- @name GetLiteralTypes
-- @returns :many
SELECT 1 AS whole, 0.5 AS half, 1e10 AS huge FROM dummy
schema_sql: CREATE TABLE dummy (id SERIAL PRIMARY KEY)
